actions.action: Lift plant out of decorative pot and empty standing water
If soil is dry, water thoroughly and let drain
Trim dead, crispy, yellow or brown stems and leaves
Cut green stems into 4-6 inch cuttings with 2 nodes and place in water or moist mix in bright indirect light
If roots are healthy, repot into 2-inch-wider pot with drainage and aroid mix
Trim any rotted roots before repotting
Ongoing: water only when top 2 inches of soil are dry and ensure pot drains

reason: The answer blames a root-bound plant with dieback rather than overgrown leggy growth needing a hard cut-back. Its chop-and-prop and repot steps overlap the fix but focus on removing dead material and propagation, not an explicit 60-80% trim of the mother plant. Nothing it recommends is harmful.
